branch.new_demand: Prove why the construction works and derive the inradius formula.

questions.skill: Prove that the incenter is equidistant from the sides
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: The bisectors of ∠A and ∠B of △ABC meet at I. Prove that I is equidistant from all three sides and lies on the bisector of ∠C.
questions.prompt_markup: The bisectors of ∠A and ∠B of △ABC meet at I. Prove that I is equidistant from all three sides and lies on the bisector of ∠C.
questions.correct_answer: I is equidistant from AB, BC, CA and lies on the bisector of ∠C.
questions.required_method: Use the angle bisector distance property twice, then its converse at C.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: on the bisector of ∠A: d(I, AB) = d(I, AC); on the bisector of ∠B: d(I, AB) = d(I, BC); so d(I, AC) = d(I, BC); the converse puts I on the bisector of ∠C.
